title: Supramolecular Assembly of an Antimicrobial Peptide Into a Pore
abstract: ABSTRACT Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) have long been ascribed the ability to form pores. These structures, some observed, others inferred, vary in their mechanisms of action, though most are associated with lysis. Here, we show that an AMP derived from a truncated staphylococcal δ‐toxin can form functional pores that do not cause rapid lysis but, instead, we suggest that they act as self‐transport systems. Specifically, a 17‐amino acid AMP named STIP3‐1 was observed to oligomerize and form a unique supramolecular helical assembly with an ∼14 Å pore. Substitutions to the STIP3‐1 peptide abolished our ability to detect pore formation in model membranes and prevented peptide accumulation in Staphylococcus aureus . In the case of G3A and G3Aib variants, the substitutions resulted in stabilization of antiparallel 4‐helix bundles rather than a nanotubular assembly characterized by a two‐ring structure formed by repeating trimers. MD simulations suggest that Gly may impart versatility in STIP3‐1 phospholipid binding. Our observation of this remarkable STIP3‐1 structure expands how we can approach mechanistic and translational studies of AMPs.

title: Early Multicenter Experience with the Nexus DuoTM Aortic Arch Stent Graft System in the Treatment of Aneurysmatic Aortic Arch Diseases.
abstract: Objective The Nexus Duo endograft is a novel device designed for endovascular repair of aneurysmal disease of the aortic arch (EAAR). It features a dedicated indwelling branch for the brachiocephalic trunk and a customized retrograde branch for either the left common carotid artery (LCCA) or left subclavian artery (LSA). This study evaluates the early clinical outcomes of the Nexus Duo endograft in EAAR.Methods This multicenter, observational, physician-sponsored registry retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected data from nine European centers. All consecutive patients who underwent EAAR with the Nexus Duo endograft between January 2023 and April 2025 were included in the study. The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality. Secondary endpoints included technical success, overall reinterventions, major adverse events (MAEs), and the incidence of endoleaks at 30 days.Results Thirty patients (53% female) were treated. Indications for EAAR included non-dissecting aneurysm (n=7, 23.3%), post-type-B-dissection aneurysm (n=7, 23.3%), post-type-A-dissection aneurysm (n=14, 46.7%), false aneurysm (n=1, 3.3%), and penetrating ulcer (n=1, 3.3%). The LSA was the target vessel in 17 patients (56.7%). Seventeen patients underwent simultaneous LCCA-LSA bypass (58.6% using polytetrafluoroethylene grafts). Technical success was 100%. At 30 days, the mortality rate was 3.3% (n=1), the reintervention rate was 16.7%, and the MAE rate was 6.7%. No disabling strokes were observed. One transient ischemic attack occurred and one type Ia endoleak (3.3%) were observed at 30 days.Conclusions In this real-world, multicentre study, the Nexus Duo endograft demonstrated a favorable early safety profile, with high technical success, no disabling strokes, and encouraging 30-day outcomes.

title: Knockout of odourant receptor co-receptor HvarOrco compromises reproductive fitness in the ladybird Hippodamia variegata
abstract: Abstract The predatory ladybird, Hippodamia variegata , relies critically on olfaction for host location, oviposition site selection, and predator avoidance. Here, we employed CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing to generate a stable, heritable odourant receptor co-receptor ( Orco ) knockout line ( HvarOrco − /− ). Electrophysiological assessment using electroantennogram (EAG) recordings revealed that homozygous mutants exhibited profound anosmia, with significantly attenuated responses to six key semiochemicals, including the aphid alarm pheromone E -β-farnesene. Consistent with these physiological deficits, Y-tube assays demonstrated a complete loss of behavioural attraction towards host-associated cues in both sexes. Crucially, we uncovered a severe fitness cost associated with Orco deficiency. Mating assays revealed a sexual dimorphism in reproductive behaviour: while mutant females mated successfully, HvarOrco −/− males exhibited a significant failure to initiate copulation. Furthermore, post-copulatory reproductive output was drastically compromised; mutant pairs showed a 68.4% reduction in fecundity (10.3 ± 0.51 vs. 32.6 ± 0.96 eggs/30d) and a 90.4% decline in egg hatchability (8% ± 2% vs. 83% ± 1%). These findings establish HvarOrco as a dual determinant of both ecological adaptation and reproductive success. Collectively, our study validates a robust CRISPR/Cas9-based functional genomics platform for this ecologically important family of natural enemies and highlights the need for further investigation into potential non-canonical roles of this conserved co-receptor in reproductive physiology.

title: Electrochemical Cytokine Profiling Reveals Dual Immunomodulatory Effects of Human Milk Oligosaccharides in THP-1 Macrophages
abstract: Abstract Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are bioactive carbohydrates that govern host–microbe interactions and immune regulation. Beyond their antimicrobial and antibiofilm functions, HMOs have been shown to modulate inflammatory pathways by altering cytokine expression, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), which are key mediators in infection and inflammation associated complications. In this study, we characterize the effects of HMOs on cytokine secretion in THP-1 macrophages stimulated with lipopolysaccharides using a validated magnetic bead electrochemical sandwich assay (MBESA). The electrochemical assay enabled precise quantification of cytokine responses and revealed that HMO treatment attenuated proinflammatory signaling in LPS stimulated macrophages. These findings provide new insights into the immunomodulatory properties of HMOs and demonstrate the utility of electrochemical biosensing platforms for rapid, sensitive assessment of cellular inflammatory responses. Future studies will expand this approach to microphysiological systems to further elucidate HMO mediated regulation of immune signaling.

title: A COMPARATIVE CLINICAL STUDY ON THE EFFICACY OF KOLAKULATHADI CHURNA PINDA SWEDA VERSUS INFRA-RED RADIATION THERAPY IN THE MANAGEMENT OF JANU SANDHIGATA VATA (KNEE OSTEOARTHRITIS)
abstract: Background: Janu Sandhigata Vata, correlated with Knee Osteoarthritis (OA), is one of the most prevalent Vatavyadhis affecting the geriatric and middle-aged population, caused by Dhatukshaya and Vataprakopa. Knee OA affects 22–39% of the Indian population, with no proven disease-modifying agents available in conventional medicine. Kolakulathadi Churna Pinda Sweda, a form of Sankara Sweda combining Snehana and Swedana, and Infra-Red Radiation (IRR) therapy, a physiotherapy modality, are two widely used non-invasive interventions for this condition. Objective: To compare the efficacy of Kolakulathadi Churna Pinda Sweda (Group A) and Infra-Red Radiation Therapy (Group B) in the management of Janu Sandhigata Vata. Materials and Methods: An open-label comparative clinical study was conducted on 40 diagnosed patients of Janu Sandhigata Vata, allocated equally into two groups of 20 each. Group A received Kolakulathadi Churna Pinda Sweda and Group B received Infra-Red Radiation Therapy, both for 7 consecutive days, with assessment before treatment (BT), after treatment (AT, Day 7) and at follow-up (FU, Day 14). Subjective parameters (Sandhishoola, Sandhi Stabdhata, WOMAC Pain/Stiffness/Pain on Movement) and objective parameters (Sparshashayata, Sandhi Sphutana, Goniometer Flexion & Extension) were graded on a 0–3 scale. Data were analysed using paired and unpaired t-tests. Results: Both groups showed statistically highly significant improvement (p<0.001) in all nine parameters within the group. On between-group comparison, Group A showed significantly better outcomes in 2 of 9 parameters at AT and 4 of 9 parameters at FU. Overall, 50% of patients in Group A achieved marked improvement compared to only 5% in Group B. Conclusion: Both therapies are effective in Janu Sandhigata Vata; however, Kolakulathadi Churna Pinda Sweda demonstrated superior and more sustained relief compared to Infra-Red Radiation Therapy, attributable to its synergistic Snehana-Swedana action and deeper tissue penetration.

title: 227. A Diet Supplemented with Antioxidants and A Prebiotic Showed Renal Protective Benefits in Aging Cats.
abstract: Abstract Aging is a major risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD) in cats, characterized by progressive changes in renal biomarkers, hematologic indices, and body composition. The objective of this retrospective study was to evaluate whether a dietary nutrient blend containing antioxidants, fatty acids, and chicory root, could mitigate age-associated changes in markers related to renal health in aging cats. A portion of this study has been previously published (Cupp et al., 2007; Cupp et al., 2008). Ninety healthy mixed-breed cats aged 7–17 yr were housed individually and fed one of three nutritionally complete diets for the remainder of life: a control diet (CON), control plus antioxidants (vitamin E and β carotene; AOX), or control plus antioxidants, chicory root, and linoleic fatty acid (AOX+). Cats were blocked by age, sex, and body condition score and randomly assigned to treatment. Blood chemistry, complete blood count, body weight, body condition score, and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry outcomes were collected longitudinally. Data were analyzed using linear or quadratic longitudinal models to account for age and attrition, with significance declared at P ≤ 0.05 and trends at 0.05 0.10), resulting in higher hematocrit values compared to CON (P < 0.05). Body weight loss over time occurred in all groups; however, AOX+ cats experienced a reduced rate of weight loss compared with controls (P ≤ 0.05). These biomarkers and outcomes are commonly associated with renal function and the onset or progression of CKD in cats. In conclusion, long-term feeding of a diet containing antioxidants, fatty acids, and chicory root mitigated multiple age-associated directional biomarker changes linked to declining renal health. These findings support the use of this nutrient blend to help maintain markers of healthy kidney function in aging cats.

title: Evaluation of Age-Related Periodontal Inflammatory Burden Using PISA: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate age-related differences in periodontal inflammatory burden among systemically healthy patients with periodontitis using Periodontal Inflamed Surface Area (PISA) and conventional periodontal clinical parameters.Materials and MethodsThis retrospective cross-sectional study included 72 systemically healthy patients aged 25–64 years who were diagnosed with Stage III–IV periodontitis. Participants were categorized into three age groups: 25–44, 45–54, and 55–64 years. PISA values were calculated using routinely recorded PPD and BOP data from six sites per tooth. Intergroup comparisons were performed using Kruskal–Wallis and Mann–Whitney U tests. title: IMPACT OF PRE-OPERATIVE DUPLEX MAPPING ON AV FISTULA MATURATION RATES
abstract: Background: Arteriovenous (AV) fistula is still considered the access of choice for hemodialysis owing to its better long-term patency rates and associated complications compared to grafts and catheters. Nonetheless, primary non-maturity has remained an important drawback, contributing to, or rather resulting in, delays in starting patients with hemodialysis, along with increased hospital expenditures. Pre-operative duplex ultrasound mapping has been advised for better selection, but its use has been inconsistent, with downstream realities, or evidence, still emerging. Aims: Assess the impact that pre-operative duplex ultrasound mapping has on the maturation rates and medium-term patency of AV fistulas for first-time AV fistula patients. Method: This present study compared the outcomes among first-time AV fistula patients undergoing pre-operative duplex ultrasound mapping and those who went to fistula creation guided solely by clinical examination at King Hussein Medical Center (KHMC) in the periods betweem January 2024 and December 2025. The primary outcome was the functional maturation of fistula. Secondary outcomes included access-related revisions early and patency of fistula at 6 and 12 months, respectively. Demographic, clinical, and procedural variables was analyzed for their association with access outcomes. Results: Among 608 patients, 324 (53.3%) underwent pre-operative duplex mapping. Functional maturation occurred in 75.3% of mapped versus 71.1% of unmapped fistulas (P=0.245). After adjustment, duplex mapping was associated with higher odds of maturation (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.02–2.40; P=0.039) and a lower risk of primary patency loss (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.60–0.99; P=0.046). Mapping was not associated with early or 12-month revision rates. Conclusion: Duplex preoperative mapping showed to be beneficial in terms of increasing the rate of AVF maturation, but it might also lead to an increase in patency. However, one should approach these results carefully.

title: IN-VITRO ASSESSMENT OF THE EFFECT OF CURCUMIN ON PROTHROMBIN TIME AND ACTIVATED PARTIAL THROMBOPLASTIN TIME IN NORMAL PLASMA
abstract: Curcumin is the main polyphenolic constituent of Curcuma longa and has been credited with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticoagulant properties in a range of experimental settings. Even so, its influence on the routine clotting screens used in clinical laboratories has not been fully characterized. The research conducted to determine whether increasing concentrations of curcumin alter Prothrombin Time (PT) and Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) when added directly to normal human plasma. Fifty apparently healthy volunteers donated citrated blood, from which platelet-poor plasma (PPP) was separated. PT and APTT were recorded on each plasma sample first without additive and then again after spiking with curcumin at 1%, 2%, and 4%, using a semi-automated coagulation analyzer. Mean PT rose from a baseline of 14.01 ± 1.184 seconds to 14.27 ± 1.331, 14.62 ± 1.425, and 15.30 ± 1.564 seconds at the three respective concentrations. Mean APTT followed the same upward trend, moving from 32.69 ± 1.801 seconds at baseline to 33.03 ± 1.844, 33.51 ± 1.894, and 34.42 ± 1.970 seconds. Pearson correlation coefficients between concentration and clotting time ranged from 0.930 to 0.973 (P < 0.001) across all comparisons. It is concluded that Curcumin lengthened both PT and APTT in a dose-related fashion, pointing to an inhibitory action on both the extrinsic and intrinsic arms of the coagulation cascade.

title: Enriched and highly functional mucosal-associated invariant T cells in follicular fluid of patients with polycystic ovary syndrome
abstract: Abstract Background The involvement of mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) has not been adequately studied, and their potential as therapeutic targets remains unexplored. In this study, we investigated the immune profile of MAIT cells in the localized ovarian inflammatory milieu of patients with PCOS and explored their association with the inflammatory manifestations of this condition. Methods Follicular fluid samples were obtained from 20 patients with PCOS and 18 controls (women with male-factor infertility) undergoing in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (IVF/ICSI) between May and December 2023. Paired peripheral blood samples were collected before oocyte retrieval. Mononuclear cells were isolated from both compartments, and flow cytometry was used to assess MAIT cell frequency, phenotype, and cytokine production. Correlations with clinical parameters were also evaluated. Results Circulating MAIT cells from patients with PCOS showed a reduced frequency but exhibited an activated phenotype characterized by elevated of CD38, PD-1, and TIGIT expression. Notably, MAIT cells were enriched in the follicular fluid of patients with PCOS, where they expressed high levels of PD-1 and CD38 and secreted higher amounts of IFN-γ and IL-17A, suggesting the presence of both MAIT1 and MAIT17 subsets within the ovarian inflammatory milieu. Conclusions MAIT cells are enriched in the follicular fluid of patients with PCOS and display an activated, proinflammatory phenotype with enhanced IFN-γ and IL-17A production. The correlations between MAIT cell parameters and AMH and BMI, together with the association between MAIT cell-derived IL-17A and testosterone, suggest a potential link between the local enrichment of MAIT cells and the inflammatory and hormonal milieu in PCOS, although the directionality of these associations remains to be determined.

title: Optimized L1CAM-CAR T cells enhance activity against moderate-antigen-density rhabdomyosarcoma models.
abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), the most common pediatric soft tissue sarcoma, remains difficult to treat in relapsed, metastatic, or refractory disease. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has demonstrated promising results in hematological diseases, but its application to solid tumors including RMS is limited by antigen heterogeneity, on-target/off-tumor toxicity, and insufficient activity against moderate antigen density. We investigated L1 cell adhesion molecule (L1CAM) as a candidate CAR T cell target in RMS by profiling expression in cell lines, patient-derived xenografts, and healthy tissues. Using the CE7-derived single-chain variable fragment, we engineered and compared L1CAM-CAR constructs differing in hinge and costimulatory domains, including the clinically tested 4-1BB-based CE7-CAR configuration. Functional activity was assessed across fusion-positive and fusion-negative RMS models in vitro and in orthotopic mouse models, with B7-H3-CAR T cells included as a benchmark. L1CAM was expressed at variable but specific levels across RMS models, with more prominent expression in fusion-positive RMS and limited expression in healthy tissues. Among constructs, the CD28-based L1CAM.III-CAR showed the strongest cytotoxicity and IFN-γ release, including partial activity in a low-L1CAM model. In vivo, L1CAM.III-CAR T cells improved expansion, delayed tumor progression, and prolonged survival compared with the clinical-reference L1CAM.CT construct, although responses were incomplete and less pronounced than those achieved with B7-H3-CAR T cells. These findings support L1CAM as a rational target for L1CAM-positive RMS cases and demonstrate that CAR optimization can enhance activity against moderate-density antigens. The potent antitumor activity and favorable selectivity profile of L1CAM.III-CAR T cells support their development for pediatric sarcoma immunotherapy.

title: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia Type 11: A Comprehensive Case Report.
abstract: Hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) is a heterogeneous group of genetically determined diseases, characterized by progressive spastic paraparesis of the lower limbs, associated with degeneration of the corticospinal tract and the posterior column of the spinal cord. Currently known to be about 70 genes are involved in HSP, though new potentially pathogenic variants are being reported regularly. Almost all patterns of inheritance like autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked, and mitochondrial have been found in families of HSP patients. However, autosomal recessive form, hereditary spastic paraplegia type 11 is the most common one. We presented a case of an 18-year-old woman, with no significant medical history and without known consanguinity, presented with a 2-year history of sub-acute onset and slowly progressing weakness and stiffness in both lower limbs and difficulty in walking and finally diagnosed as a Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia 11. Genetic analysis by whole-exome sequencing on the Illumina Novaseq 6000 NGS Platform was done and indicated homozygous variations in exon 4 of gene SPG11(chr15:g.44657230_44657231delAT): the c733_734del p (Met245ValfsTer2) variant on the allele. Here, we describe the clinical, radiological, and genetic presentation of Spastic paraplegia 11 (SPG11) through a report of a case and compare it with previously reported SPG11 cases in the literature.

title: Factors Influencing Person-Centered Nursing of Clinical Psychiatric Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Descriptive Survey Study
abstract: Purpose: This study examined the effects of job engagement, emotional labor, self-efficacy for counseling skills, and social interest on the person-centered nursing of clinical psychiatric nurses.Methods: This descriptive study included 194 clinical psychiatric nurses from 11 psychiatric institutions who had worked for at least one year. Data were collected from January 20 to March 16, 2025, using structured questionnaires. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson's correlation coefficients, and multiple stepwise regression analysis.Results: The factor with the greatest influence on person-centered nursing was social interest (β=.48, p<.001), followed by self-efficacy for counseling skills (β=.31, p<.001), 5-15 years of clinical psychiatric nursing experience (β=-.12, p=.020), and holding a head nurse position (β=.12, p=.024). The regression model was statistically significant (F=55.43, p<.001), and these four variables explained 53% of the variance in person-centered nursing.Conclusion: To enhance the person-centered nursing of clinical psychiatric nurses, it is necessary to develop and implement educational and intervention programs aimed at strengthening their social interest and self-efficacy for counseling skills. Furthermore, tailored educational strategies and organizational support systems that reflect nurses' clinical career stages and job positions should be established to further promote person-centered nursing.
venue: Journal of Korean Academy of Psychiatric and Mental Health Nursing

title: ASSESSMENT OF ADR DETECTION, REPORTING AWARENESS, AND RISK PERCEPTION AMONG PHARMACY STUDENTS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL INSTITUTIONAL STUDY
abstract: Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are an important concern in healthcare and can contribute to patient morbidity, mortality, increased healthcare costs, and prolonged hospital stay. Pharmacovigilance plays an important role in identifying, monitoring, assessing, and preventing adverse effects associated with medicines. ADR reporting is an important part of pharmacovigilance because it helps in detecting safety problems that may not be identified during clinical trials. Pharmacy students are future healthcare professionals and should have adequate knowledge about ADR detection, reporting procedures, and pharmacovigilance systems. The present study was conducted to assess ADR detection knowledge, reporting awareness, risk perception, and reporting practices among pharmacy students. A descriptive cross sectional institutional study was conducted among 400 pharmacy students over a period of three months. A structured, self-administered questionnaire was used for data collection. The questionnaire consisted of four sections covering demographic characteristics, ADR detection knowledge, ADR reporting awareness, and risk perception and reporting practices. The findings showed that 77.3% of respondents correctly identified the definition of an ADR, while 82.5% were aware of the WHO definition of ADR. About 71.5% were aware of ADR classification types and 77.8% reported that they could identify clinical signs of common ADRs. However, only 63.7% were familiar with causality assessment scales. Regarding reporting awareness, 81.3% recognized that ADR reporting is important for patient safety, 69.5% knew where ADRs could be reported in India, and 72.3% were familiar with the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI). However, misconceptions were observed regarding who can report ADRs and the appropriate reporting timeframe. Regarding practice, 60.9% of students had observed an ADR during clinical practice, whereas 53% had reported an ADR. ADR Monitoring Centres were the most commonly used reporting channel. A large majority of respondents, 81%, supported mandatory pharmacovigilance and ADR reporting training in the pharmacy curriculum. The study indicates that pharmacy students have generally good basic knowledge and awareness regarding ADRs, but gaps remain in practical reporting knowledge and reporting behaviour. Regular pharmacovigilance education, practical ADR reporting exercises, clinical exposure, and awareness programmes may help improve ADR reporting practices among pharmacy students.
authors: J. Peter Prince*, V. Chandru, D. Dhanush Kumar, R. Dhanushkumar, S. Premkumar, R. Manivannan

title: 324. Behavioral Responses of Impaired Feedlot Cattle After Chronic Pen Entry and Associations with Time to Death.
abstract: Abstract In feedlots, chronically impaired cattle are often moved to specialized pens, where they have easier access to resources and to facilitate monitoring and care. Understanding how chronic cattle transition into this new environment may provide insights into their likelihood of recovery. The objectives of this study were to 1) describe the behavioral time budget of chronic cattle in the first 30 min after pen entry, and 2) determine associations between these behavioral variables and time to death. Continuous video of two chronic pens at a 50,000-head commercial feedyard in Alberta, Canada, was recorded on three cameras per pen. Behaviors of 36 focal cattle, individually identified with collars, were recorded for the first 30 min after entry to the chronic pen over a 1 year period (February 2024 to 2025). Behaviors assessed included posture (standing, lying) and active behaviors (feeding, drinking, walking, social interactions, grooming, and standing other or out of view (SO)). Final disposition, diagnosis (bovine respiratory disease (BRD), lame, and other), sex, and season were recorded for each animal and used for stratified random focal animal selection. Number of days from pen entry to final disposition were also recorded. Of the 36 focal cattle, 19 (53%) recovered and 17 (47%) died. Fourteen (39%) cattle had BRD (seven recovered, seven died), 15 (42%) were lame (six recovered, nine died) and seven (19%) had other diagnoses (six recovered, one died). For Objective 1, the behaviors most commonly observed were SO, standing at the feed bunk, lying idle, and walking (averaging 44%, 30%, 14%, and 10% of time, respectively). For Objective 2, data were analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model with backwards elimination to assess behavioral and other predictors (diagnosis, season, sex) of time to death. The final model retained only a possible trend (p = 0.09), where a greater proportion of time walking during the first 30 min after pen entry was associated with a lower hazard of death. All other variables were non-significant (p > 0.10). Chronic cattle in this study spent most of their time in the first 30 min after pen entry either standing not engaged in any behaviors of interest (SO) or at the feed bunk. Greater walking time showed a trend toward a reduced hazard of death. Behavior observations at additional time points relative to pen entry, such as first feed delivery or the day after entry, should be investigated to determine if behavioral differences appear after cattle have spent more time in the chronic pen.

title: Effect of Professional Prophylaxis on Clinical Parameters and Patient Comfort: Randomized Split‐Mouth Clinical Trial
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The removal of soft and hard plaque from dental surfaces using manual and mechanical instruments is a regular part of dental practice for the control and prevention of oral diseases. To achieve this goal in a less invasive and more comfortable manner for the patient, the Guided Biofilm Therapy protocol was developed. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of the Guided Biofilm Therapy (test) protocol versus the traditional scaling protocol on short-term gingival health parameters and patient comfort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A blind randomized, split-mouth clinical trial was performed on healthy patients. Each patient was instrumented in two opposing alternate quadrants (1st and 3rd quadrants and 2nd and 4th quadrants) using the two methods under evaluation. A questionnaire was carried out using a Likert scale to measure the comfort felt by the patient during instrumentation. Plaque and bleeding indexes were evaluated at 1 and 3 weeks. RESULTS: Both protocols were associated with short-term improvements in bacterial plaque and gingival inflammation throughout the follow-up evaluations. However, no statistically significant differences were found between protocols for the clinical parameters assessed. The main difference observed was higher comfort during instrumentation with the test protocol (p = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Within the short follow-up of this study, the findings do not demonstrate clinical superiority of the Guided Biofilm Therapy protocol over the conventional protocol for gingival health parameters. The main observed difference relates to greater patient comfort during treatment.

title: ANXIOLYTIC ACTIVITY OF AQUEOUS AND ALCOHOLIC WHOLE-PLANT EXTRACTS OF GRANGEA MADERASPATANA L. IN MICE AND RATS
abstract: Background: Grangea maderaspatana (L.) Poir. (Asteraceae), traditionally used as a stomachic, sedative and carminative, has been pharmacologically studied for its oestrogenic, antifertility, analgesic, anti-inflammatory, antiarthritic, cytotoxic, antioxidant, hepatoprotective and antimicrobial activity, but its anxiolytic potential has not been systematically evaluated. Aim: To evaluate the anxiolytic activity of aqueous (AQEWGM) and alcoholic (ALEWGM) whole-plant extracts of G. maderaspatana. Materials and Methods: AQEWGM and ALEWGM were prepared by cold maceration and screened for phytoconstituents. Acute oral toxicity was assessed in mice up to 2000 mg/kg (OECD 420), and three doses (100, 200 and 400 mg/kg, p.o.) were selected. Anxiolytic activity was evaluated using the staircase, elevated plus-maze, hole-board and mirror-chamber tests in mice and rats, with diazepam (2 mg/kg) as standard. Results: Both extracts were non-toxic up to 2000 mg/kg. AQEWGM and ALEWGM (100-400 mg/kg) significantly increased steps climbed and rearings in the staircase test; increased open-arm entries/time and reduced closed-arm entries/time in the elevated plus-maze without altering total arm entries; increased head-dips, time in head-dips and rearings while reducing latency to first head-dip and defecation in the hole-board test (with a comparatively weaker effect of ALEWGM on head-dipping itself); and reduced latency to enter while increasing entries into, and time spent in, the mirror chamber - effects broadly comparable to diazepam. AQEWGM was consistently more active than ALEWGM across all four models. Phytochemical screening showed carbohydrates, steroids/triterpenoids and flavonoids in both extracts, with saponins additionally present in ALEWGM. Conclusion: Whole-plant extracts of G. maderaspatana possess significant anxiolytic-like activity across four behavioural paradigms, plausibly related to their terpenoid, steroid, flavonoid and saponin content, supporting further mechanistic investigation of the plant as a source of anxiolytic leads.
authors: Venkat Rao1 P. B. Ashwini N.*1

title: The Least Understood Placental Galectins: Galectin-14 and Galectin-16 in Human Pregnancy and Placental Biology
abstract: Galectins represent a family of proteins which are capable of specifically binding to beta-galactoside-containing sugar molecules, known as glycans. Galectins possess carbohydrate recognition domains (CRDs) that fundamentally determine their ability to bind to sugars. Galectin-14 (Gal-14) and galectin-16 (Gal-16) are members of the galectin family that is particularly associated with the placenta. The galectins in the placenta constitute a specialized subgroup functioning at the maternal–fetal interface. They are expressed primarily in the syncytiotrophoblasts. This trophoblast layer is in direct contact with maternal blood and plays a crucial role in the metabolic, hormonal and immunological interactions between the fetus and the pregnant woman. In order to prepare this structured narrative review, we conducted a structured literature search across the MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science Core Collection databases; the final search has been performed on 1 July 2026. The search strategy has combined the terms galectin-14/LGALS14 and galectin-16/LGALS16 with terms related to the placenta, trophoblast, pregnancy, placentation and pregnancy complications. Search results were imported into Mendeley Reference Manager to remove duplicates, and the reference lists of relevant review articles and studies were manually screened. Two reviewers (Z.K. and A.S.) independently screened the titles and abstracts and subsequently evaluated the potentially relevant full-text articles. The final evidence synthesis included primary studies that directly investigated the expression, function, regulation, or clinical associations of LGALS14 or LGALS16; secondary publications were used for background and contextual information. In experimental studies, galectin-14 has been linked to trophoblast migration and invasion—involving mechanisms such as the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, MMP-9 and N-cadherin—as well as to the modulation of activated maternal immune cell function. Galectin-16 is structurally more distinct and exhibits reduced classical β-galactoside-binding capacity; it appears to be closely associated with trophoblast differentiation and syncytialization, presumably through intracellular protein interactions. Altered expression of placenta-specific galectins has been observed in preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction; however, the causal relationship remains unclear. Clinical evidence regarding their use as biomarkers is emerging at this time; therefore, neither galectin-14 nor galectin-16 can be currently considered as a validated, clinically applicable biomarker. Altogether, available evidence mandates further study of galectin-14 and galectin-16, as they may be important regulators of placental biology and potential biomarker candidates. However, their physiological functions and clinical utility have not yet been sufficiently confirmed; therefore, further prospective and functional studies are required. The strongest putative mechanistic link to the development of preeclampsia exists for galectin-14, primarily involving trophoblast migration and invasion as well as PI3K/Akt-related signaling pathways. In contrast, evidence in connection with the direct role of galectin-16 is limited at present.

title: Management of Combined Vascular Malformations.
abstract: Combined vascular malformations are complex, heterogeneous lesions increasingly classified by anatomic components and genetic drivers, specifically the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway (PROS) and RASA1 mutations. These syndromes, including Klippel-Trenaunay, CLOVES, and capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation, present with soft-tissue hypertrophy, skeletal overgrowth, and varied vascular anomalies. Effective management requires a multidisciplinary approach to address complications such as thromboembolism, localized intravascular coagulopathy, and limb-length discrepancy. Diagnostic evaluation relies on ultrasound and MRI. Therapeutic interventions have evolved from conservative compression and sclerotherapy to targeted pharmacotherapy (sirolimus, alpelisib) and individualized surgical debulking, with the aim of improving functional outcomes and quality of life.

title: Fluid–structure interaction dynamics of cervical lymphatic vessel pumping and valvular function
abstract: A substantial portion of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) drains through cervical lymphatic vessels (CLVs), a pathway mediated by basal and dorsal meningeal lymphatics. Impaired drainage along this route has been implicated in ageing, Alzheimer's disease and traumatic brain injury. Despite considerable experimental investigation of CLV structure and function, computational modelling of this pathway remains limited. Here, we present a fully coupled two-dimensional fluid-structure interaction (FSI) model of a murine CLV constructed using the lattice Boltzmann method for fluid dynamics and the immersed boundary method for the vessel geometry. Distinct from previous lymphatic vessel models, this framework is parametrized using data from recent in vivo imaging studies of CLVs. Using this model, we characterize the transient FSI dynamics within a single lymphangion, the pumping performance across a chain of three lymphangions with varying contraction phase delays and the role of circular sinus geometry in regulating CSF transport under both favourable and adverse pressure gradients. Our results provide the first high-fidelity simulation of CSF drainage through CLVs, bridging a gap between experimental observations and mechanistic understanding. This work offers new insights into CLV pumping behaviour and valve function, which helps inform the design of future experiments and therapeutic strategies aimed at enhancing CSF clearance.
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface

title: Food System, Poverty, and Malnutrition in Bangladesh: Challenges and Policy Implications
abstract: The interconnections among food systems, poverty, and malnutrition remain central to Bangladesh’s development trajectory. Despite substantial agricultural growth and notable reductions in poverty over the past two decades, structural challenges continue to constrain equitable access to food and nutrition. This study analyzes agricultural production trends, food system drivers, and consumption behaviors, situating Bangladesh in a comparative South Asian context. Using national survey data and secondary statistics, it further examines poverty dynamics, both income-based and multidimensional and their implications for food insecurity and nutrition outcomes. The empirical evidence highlights persistent disparities in dietary diversity, caloric intake, and affordability of healthy diets across rural–urban and socio-economic groups. Moreover, the prevalence of child undernutrition and the double burden of malnutrition underscore the fragility of current nutrition gains. The findings suggest that external shocks, including climate variability, market volatility, and global food price fluctuations, exacerbate systemic vulnerabilities. Policy analysis indicates that while government interventions in agriculture, poverty alleviation, and nutrition have achieved incremental success, gaps remain in coordination, targeting, and long-term sustainability. The paper argues for integrated, multisectoral strategies that enhance agricultural productivity, strengthen social protection mechanisms, and promote resilient, nutrition-sensitive food systems. Such approaches are essential to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) on zero hunger, poverty reduction, and improved health outcomes in Bangladesh.

title: 79. Detection of Sow Feeding- and Drinking-related Behaviors in Farrowing Crates Using Oriented Bounding Boxes.
abstract: Abstract Sow feeding and drinking behavior during farrowing can provide useful management information, but continuous observation is difficult in commercial systems because of labor constraints and herd size. Camera-based monitoring offers a scalable alternative, although detection from overhead farrowing-crate images is complicated when sows are positioned diagonally relative to the camera frame. In those cases, conventional axis-aligned bounding boxes may include substantial background near the feeder or drinker, which can hinder discrimination among visually similar behaviors. This study evaluated the use of oriented bounding boxes for detecting sow feeding- and drinking-related behaviors from overhead video recorded in individual farrowing crates. The study was conducted at the Imported Swine Research Laboratory at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign across three farrowing trials involving 24 sows, with one overhead camera per crate. Video frames were annotated into three classes: Active_Feeding, At_Feeder_Not_Feeding, and Drinking. A total of 228 images from two trials were used for model development, and 54 images from the remaining trial, representing eight sows, were reserved for independent evaluation. Hyperparameters were selected using a structured grid search during model development. On the held-out trial, the model achieved 0.84 precision, 0.91 recall, and 0.91 mean average precision. Drinking showed the highest recall, whereas At_Feeder_Not_Feeding had lower precision, likely because of visual similarity to active feeding. These results support the feasibility of using oriented bounding boxes to detect feeding- and drinking-related behaviors in overhead farrowing-crate images. Additional testing with larger and more diverse datasets is needed to determine robustness and comparative performance against conventional annotation approaches.
authors: Isabella Cardoso Ferreira da Silva Condotta

title: Effectiveness of Manual and Triple-Headed Toothbrushes in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
abstract: Background: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) frequently experience difficulties in maintaining adequate oral hygiene due to sensory sensitivities, impaired motor coordination, and resistance to conventional toothbrushing techniques1. Alternative toothbrush designs may help improve plaque control and brushing efficiency in this population.Aim: To assess and compare the effectiveness of manual and triple-headed toothbrushes in children with autism spectrum disorderMaterials and Methods: Forty children diagnosed with ASD were randomly allocated into two groups (n = 20 each). Group A used a triple-headed toothbrush, while Group B used a conventional single-headed manual toothbrush. Oral hygiene status was assessed using the Simplified Oral Hygiene Index (OHI-S) at baseline and after two weeks of supervised toothbrushing. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate parametric or non-parametric tests.Results: Both groups showed a statistically significant reduction in OHI-S scores after two weeks. The triple-headed toothbrush group demonstrated a greater reduction in mean OHI-S scores compared to the single-headed toothbrush group.Conclusion: Triple-headed toothbrushes may be a more effective alternative for improving oral hygiene in children with ASD, particularly where manual dexterity and brushing compliance are limited.

title: Cytokine Concentrations in Seminal Plasma and Blood in HIV Infection: Differential Modulation by Antiretroviral Therapy and Association with HIV RNA Levels and CD4+T Cell Count
abstract: Background and Objectives: The complex cytokine network in seminal fluid during human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate inflammatory cytokine levels in the semen of individuals with chronic HIV infection and assess the effects of antiretroviral therapy ART on cytokine networks. Materials and Methods: A total of 26 HIV infected individuals were recruited, including 16 treatment-naïve (TN) patients, 10 patients receiving ART for over 2 years with plasma HIV viral loads of < 20 copies/mL (CR group), and 4 healthy controls (HC). Differences in inflammatory cytokine levels were analyzed using the Olink assay in paired seminal plasma and blood samples, along with correlations between cytokine levels and indicators of disease progression. Moreover, differences in cytokine networks between seminal plasma and blood plasma were analyzed, and the effects of ART on these networks were evaluated. Results: HIV infection and ART altered cytokine networks in seminal plasma compared with those in HC. The levels of semen cluster 1 (interferon-γ, IL-12B, MCP-2, MCP-4, and Flt3L) in the TN group were significantly higher than those in the HC group. HIV infection was associated with increased rigidity of the seminal cytokine network, and significant differences were observed between the cytokine networks of seminal and blood plasma, both with and without ART. Additionally, seminal plasma levels of Flt3L, MCP-4, IL-1alpha, OSM, TWEAK, VEGFA, transforming growth factor-alpha, HGF, NT-3, IL-4, IL-17C, beta-NGF, FGF-19, and TRAIL were significantly correlated with baseline HIV RNA levels and CD4 + T cell counts. Conclusion: ART had a greater effect on cytokine levels in blood plasma than in seminal plasma. Seminal plasma also exhibited higher concentrations of cytokines associated with indicators of HIV disease progression than blood plasma. Keywords: cytokine, human immunodeficiency virus, plasma, seminal

title: The Maxillofacial Academic Practice (MAP) study phase 1: oral and maxillofacial surgical trainee research engagement.
abstract: The British Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (BAOMS) funded Maxillofacial Academic Practice (MAP) study aims to define the current state of research and academic training within UK Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (OMFS). Phase One of the study, the OMFS Trainee Research Engagement Survey, explores levels of research involvement, barriers, and facilitators among trainees. An online cross-sectional survey was developed comprising multiple-choice, free-text, and 10-point Likert scale items. It was distributed to OMFS trainees across the UK. The primary outcome was the level of research interest and current engagement, while secondary outcomes included identifying barriers, facilitators, and proposed interventions to be explored in Phase Two. A total of 82 OMFS trainees responded, representing all UK training regions and levels. Of these, 30/82 were specialist trainees and 45/82 were pre-ST3 trainees. A total of 58/82 expressed clear research interest, and 46/82 were actively involved in projects. However, only 19/82 reported working in departments with OMFS-led research, and 51/82 were unaware of local research contacts. Research interest was significantly higher among trainees in research-affiliated units. Despite the high level of interest, 25/82 reported having no opportunity to participate. Mean self-rated exposure to research was 5/10. OMFS trainees demonstrate strong academic interest, yet access to research opportunities remains limited. Trainees with greater exposure are more likely to pursue academic careers. Targeted recommendations include clearer national guidance, improved access to mentorship, and the development of cross-Deanery academic networks to support future OMFS clinical academics - as will be explored in Phase 2 of the MAP study.

title: Linguistic features from paragraph recall are markers of cognitive impairment
abstract: Abstract Objective Cognitive impairment is associated with language changes that may be elicited from verbal responses during neuropsychological assessments that are not captured in traditional scoring. The current study investigated the utility of a linguistic analysis of paragraph recall responses for differentiating participants with and without cognitive impairment. Methods Digital voice recordings of Logical Memory (LM) were available from 598 participants from the Long Life Family Study with normal cognition and 112 with cognitive impairment. Linguistic polyfeature scores for immediate (PFS-IR) and delayed recall (PFS-DR) were created from a weighted sum of features associated with cognitive impairment. Logistic regression models assessed the predictive value of each PFS and demographics for classifying cognitive impairment. Repeated measures models with Generalized Estimating Equations assessed whether PFSs predict decline on a cognitive screener. Results Both immediate and delayed PFSs were significantly associated with cognitive status (PFS-IR β = 0.05, p< .001; PFS-DR β = 0.07, p< .001). A classifier with PFS-DR and demographics closely approximated the accuracy of the traditional LM score and demographics (AUC-PR = 0.81 vs 0.84, respectively). A higher PFS-DR was also associated with greater cognitive decline over an average of 5 years of follow-up (β = -0.08, p< .001). Conclusion Quantification of linguistic features from paragraph recall using a linguistic PFS provides sufficient information for detecting cognitive impairment and predicting incident cognitive decline. The linguistic PFS has the potential to be integrated into automated testing, recording, and scoring pipelines allowing for the implementation of sensitive neuropsychological assessments in broader clinical and research settings.
venue: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society

title: WATER AS A RURAL CAPITAL
abstract: Water serves as a vital rural asset, it increases productivity and food security. It also improves public health and contributes to economic growth and poverty reduction in rural areas. Poor hygiene practices, unsafe water, restricted access to water and water services and sanitation pose serious risk to health and livelihoods. This study evaluated the role of water as a rural capital by analysing drinking water quality, household practices, health challenges in communities in Akonolinga, Cameroon. The study used a community based cross-sectional survey among 158 households across 10 villages in Akonolinga. Withe the aid of structured questionnaires, information on water sources, household income were collected. Water samples were assessed for nitrate ,nitrite, residual, chlorine and pH. WHo guidelines were used to interpret the measured parameters. Results showed firstly that 72.78% depend on farming as their main source of livelihoods, 38.61% of households used boreholes as their main source of drinking water and 62.03% of households earned less than 50,000 FCFA monthly Secondly28.48% reported that at least one child below 5years had been seriously sick during the last 6 months, an average of 2.41days was lost while caring for a child, atleast 3000 to above 6000frswas lost caring for a sick child meanwhile 54.43%of households did not treat their water before giving to infants Lastly 94.94% of tested samples had pH less than or equal to 6.8, 70.41% of the samples analysed had no residual chlorine, 42.41% of all samples recorded 3mg/L of nitrate, and 52.53% of all samples showed 0.005mg/L of nitrite. As a result of the Restitution authorities requested for the improved management of all water sources, identification of all functional and non-functional boreholes, and additional boreholess need in Akonolknga. Construction of boreholes subsequently started in Ngoubou Water is this an essential rural asset in Akonolinga. Irs access does not ensure water security. There is therefore a need for stronger community and local government action due to weakness in water management, household practices and health related economic burden.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF EMULGEL FOR TOPICAL DRUG DELIVERY
abstract: Topical drug delivery systems offer a convenient and effective mode of delivery of drugs to the skin surface, which increases local concentration of the drug while minimizing systemic adverse effects. Emulgels are considered as one of the potential dosage forms, which offer solution for topical drug delivery. They are mixtures of an emulsion and gel matrix and allow delivery of both hydrophilic and hydrophobic drugs. This article highlights a discussion on topical drug delivery and emulgels, including their types, formulating ingredients, methods of preparation, and evaluation parameters. A brief description on the anatomy of the skin and its barrier properties towards topical drug delivery is also presented. Emulgels are described with a focus on the aqueous and oily phases, emulsifying agents, permeation enhancers, and gelling agents. The physiological, physicochemical, and formulation factors that may influence topical drug absorption are also outlined. Moreover, the article discusses the various types of emulgels: macroemulgels, microemulgels, and nanoemulgels, and their characteristics such as particle size and stability. Other evaluation parameters include physical appearance, pH, viscosity, stability, irritation, and zeta potential, particle size distribution, polydispersity index, swelling index, drug content, spreadability, and extrudability. Emulgels can be used as a versatile topically applicable dosage form due to their enhanced spreading ability, patient acceptability, high drug loading, stability, and controlled release property. Future work focused on the evaluation and formulation of emulgels would be of paramount importance in topical and transdermal drug delivery.

title: 258. Evaluating Insulin Resistance and Sensitivity Values in Beef Steers from Birth to Weaning.
abstract: Abstract Although insulin status is known to affect growth and metabolic performance, it is unclear whether maternal insulin status directly affects calf insulin status at birth. Insulin resistance has been evaluated for animal performance in the feedlot but has limited research in pre-weaning calves. Additionally, there has been limited research on how dam insulin resistance relates to calf insulin resistance and performance. The objective of this study was to determine if dam insulin resistance and sensitivity values correspond to offspring insulin resistance and sensitivity values as well as performance characteristics. Steers (n = 43) and their respective dams were evaluated for insulin-related measures at the KSU Agricultural Research Center located in Hays, KS. Dam blood samples were collected after a 12 hour fast, 2 weeks before their expected calving date. Steer blood samples were collected 24 hours post birth. All blood samples were processed to obtain plasma. Individual animal was used for the experimental unit. Weights were collected both at birth (35 ± 4.2 kg) and weaning (183 ± 26.7 kg). Plasma was analyzed for insulin and glucose concentrations with corresponding values utilized to calculate the dam and steer Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR; 3.13 ±3.432, 4.90 ±4.077) and Quantitative Insulin Sensitivity Check Index (QUICKI; 0.36 ±0.062, 0.32±0.030) indices. Relationships between variables were assessed with Pearson correlation coefficients in R Studio (R-4.5.1.pkg) Effects were considered significant at P ≤ 0.05 and considered tendency when 0.05 < P ≤ 0.10. Dam QUICKI was positively correlated with steer QUICKI (r = 0.46, P = 0.002) indicating dam insulin sensitivity values may influence calf insulin sensitivity values at birth. Steer QUICKI was negatively correlated with weaning gain (r = -0.60, P < 0.001) indicating steers with lower gain had lower insulin sensitivity. Steer HOMA-IR was positively correlated with weaning gain (r = 0.52, P < 0.001) showing that steers with higher insulin resistance values had higher weaning weight gain. Dam QUICKI was negatively correlated to weaning gain (r = -0.38, P = 0.01) and tended to be negatively correlated with birth weight (r = -0.28, P = 0.07). Both indicating greater maternal insulin sensitivity is related to reduced offspring weaning gain. Dam insulin sensitivity values may be associated with calf insulin sensitivity values at birth, but they are negatively correlated with birth weight and weaning gains. Higher insulin resistance values may be associated with higher weaning gains and birth weight. These dynamics assist in explaining the key endocrine foundation that cattle may carry throughout their production. Further research is needed to determine if dam insulin sensitivity and insulin resistance values are related to steer insulin sensitivity, insulin resistance, and performance later in their production, both in backgrounding and in the feedlot.

title: Nontraumatic Dental Emergency Department Visits and Follow Up Dental Care Among Wisconsin Medicaid Beneficiaries
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Emergency department (ED) visits for nontraumatic dental conditions (NTDCs) are a persistent concern for Medicaid beneficiaries. This study examined factors associated with NTDC-related ED utilization and dental follow up among Wisconsin Medicaid beneficiaries. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective claims-based cohort study using Wisconsin Medicaid claims from January 1, 2014, through December 31, 2019. The ED cohort (n = 553,669) outcome was at least one NTDC-related ED visit. The follow up cohort (n = 21,386 with an index NTDC-related ED visit) outcome was at least one nonemergency dental visit within 6 months. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted associations. Supplementary analyses used a logistic prediction model and LightGBM under a balanced modeling framework. RESULTS: Adults had the highest NTDC-related ED visit rate (6.0%), exceeding children (1.5%) and older adults (1.5%). Rates were higher among White (4.4%) and Black (4.1%) beneficiaries than among Hispanic beneficiaries (2.7%). Only 8.8% of beneficiaries with an NTDC-related ED visit received dental follow up within 6 months. After adjustment, HMO enrollment, adult age group, and residence in non-Milwaukee urban or rural areas were associated with higher odds of NTDC-related ED visits. For follow up, the highest area level income quartile had greater odds of subsequent nonemergency dental care. CONCLUSIONS: NTDC-related ED utilization and post ED dental follow up were associated with demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and insurance related factors. The low follow up rate suggests a substantial gap between emergency care and subsequent nonemergency dental care, supporting care coordination, Medicaid dental access, and regional strategies for connecting ED patients to dental providers.

title: DOCTORS' PERSPECTIVES ON PATIENT SATISFACTION: QUALITATIVE SURVEY IN A TERTIARY HEALTH CARE FACILITY IN CHANDIGARH, INDIA
abstract: Background: Patient satisfaction is an important indicator of healthcare quality and system performance. While patient perspectives are commonly assessed, healthcare providers’ perspectives have received comparatively limited attention in India. Understanding doctors’ perceptions is important for developing effective quality-improvement strategies. Objective: To explore doctors’ perspectives regarding patient satisfaction, perceived quality of healthcare services, challenges encountered in providing patient care, and strategies for improving patient satisfaction in a tertiary-care government hospital in Chandigarh, India. Methods: An exploratory qualitative survey was conducted among doctors providing patient-care services in different outpatient departments of a tertiary-care government hospital in Chandigarh from April to December 2025. Convenience sampling was used, and 41 doctors were included. Data were collected through semi-structured personal interviews and a focus group discussion on strategies for improving patient care services was also conducted. Qualitative responses were analyzed using thematic coding, while proportions and percentages were used to describe quantitative findings. Results: Among all doctors surveyed, 87.8% considered patient satisfaction very important in evaluating quality of care, while 12.2% considered it important. Patient satisfaction surveys were considered accurate by 48.8%, very accurate by 14.6%, and somewhat accurate by 34.1% of doctors. Regular feedback was preferred directly from patients by 58.5% and through anonymized reports by 26.8%. Five major domains emerged: human resource strengthening and workload management; infrastructure and resource availability; patient communication and education; system and process reforms; and governance and policy strengthening. Human-resource shortages, excessive workload, overcrowding, inadequate infrastructure, inefficient processes, and administrative constraints were major perceived contributors to patient dissatisfaction. Conclusion: Doctors recognize patient satisfaction as an important component of healthcare quality. However, improving satisfaction requires a systems-oriented approach addressing staffing, workload, infrastructure, communication, digital processes, feedback mechanisms, and governance. Improving doctors’ working conditions and satisfaction should be considered integral to improving patient satisfaction and overall hospital performance.
authors: Dr. Dinesh Kumar*1, Dr. Naveen K. Goel2, Dr. Deepak Sharma3
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: IL27RA ubiquitination by CBL E3 ligase regulates IL27 dependent immune response against EBV- induced infectious mononucleosis
abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a trigger of robust immune responses and infectious mononucleosis (IM). Although EBV induces interleukin-27 (IL-27) in B cells, and IL-27 receptor alpha (IL27RA) deficiency increases EBV susceptibility, the regulatory mechanisms linking E3 ubiquitin ligases such as Casitas B-lineage lymphoma (CBL) to IL27RA during EBV infection remain unknown. IL27RA-interacting proteins were identified by immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry (IP-MS), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), and GST pull-down. Ubiquitination and degradation of IL27RA were assessed in human PBMCs with or without CBL overexpression. Functional assays included EBV-reactive T cell responses, flow cytometry, immunoblotting and cytokine stimulation. RNA-seq-based transcriptomic analysis was performed on IL27RA-deficient cells. CBL directly bound IL27RA, promoting its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. CBL depletion stabilized IL27RA, whereas CBL overexpression reduced IL27RA levels, suppressing STAT1/STAT3 phosphorylation and IL-27 signaling. CBL-overexpressing PBMCs showed heightened EBV-induced cell death. RNA-seq identified IL27RA-dependent dysregulation of pathways related to immune communication, hypoxia, and antiviral defense. CBL negatively regulates IL-27 signaling by degrading IL27RA, impairing antiviral immunity and exacerbating EBV immunopathogenesis. Therapeutic targeting of the CBL–IL27RA axis may benefit EBV-associated diseases.

title: POEMS Syndrome: 2026 Update on Diagnosis, Risk-Stratification, and Management.
abstract: DISEASE OVERVIEW: POEMS syndrome is a life-threatening syndrome due to an underlying plasma cell neoplasm. The major criteria for the syndrome are polyneuropathy, clonal plasma cell disorder (PCD), sclerotic bone lesions, elevated vascular endothelial growth factor, and the presence of Castleman disease. Minor features include organomegaly, endocrinopathy, characteristic skin changes, papilledema, extravascular volume overload, and thrombocytosis. DIAGNOSIS: The diagnosis of POEMS syndrome is made with three of the major criteria, two of which must include polyneuropathy and clonal plasma cell disorder, and at least one of the minor criteria. RISK STRATIFICATION: Because the pathogenesis of the syndrome is not well understood, risk stratification is limited to clinical phenotype rather than specific molecular markers. Risk factors include low serum albumin, age, pleural effusion, pulmonary hypertension, and reduced eGFR. RISK-ADAPTED THERAPY: For those patients with a dominant plasmacytoma, first line therapy is irradiation. Patients with diffuse sclerotic lesions or disseminated bone marrow involvement should receive systemic therapy. Corticosteroids are temporizing, but alkylators and lenalidomide are the mainstays of treatment, the former either in the form of low dose conventional therapy or as high-dose conditioning for stem cell transplantation. Thalidomide and bortezomib also have activity, but their benefit needs to be weighed against their risk of exacerbating the peripheral neuropathy. Daratumumab combinations also appear promising based on case series. Prompt recognition and institution of both supportive care measures and therapy directed against the plasma cell result in the best outcomes.

title: Properties of resting state functional connectivity associated with integrated combined subscales of Dark Triad
abstract: Abstract The neurobiological properties of the human brain associated with separate negative personality traits such as narcissism, psychopathy, and Machiavellianism, known as a Dark Triad (DT), have been extensively studied. However, their combinatorial properties have remained understudied in neuroimaging studies. To fill this gap, we performed a functional connectivity (FC) investigation of resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) for 129 healthy participants divided into two groups based on their profiles derived from the Dirty Dozen Dark Triad test using a clustering approach of k-means. The Variance Ratio Criterion was used to validate the optimal number of clusters. The seed-based analysis used regions of interest defined by the decrease in gray matter volume taken from a previous study. Individuals with Medium-to-High levels of Dark Triad (DT) prominence, compared to those with Low-to-Medium levels of DT, showed decreased functional connectivity between nodes of brain networks involved in emotion regulation, self-reference, and empathy. At the same time, high DT individuals demonstrated increased FC between regions involved in cognitive control and visual processing. Taken together, our findings suggest a specific and complex reconfiguration of large-scale brain networks in individuals with high DT traits rather than a generalized disruption of functional connectivity.

title: The Relationship Between Midwifery Students’Views of the Profession and Their Levels of Professional Belonging
abstract: This descriptive and correlational cross-sectional study examined the relationship between midwifery students’ views of the midwifery profession and their levels of professional belonging. The study population comprised 478 midwifery students at Karabük University. A total-enumeration approach was used; all eligible students were invited to participate, and the study was completed with 215 students who volunteered to participate (response rate: 45.0%). Data were collected using a Demographic Information Form, a descriptive questionnaire assessing students’ views of their education and the profession, and the Midwifery Belonging Scale. Analyses were performed using SPSS 22.0. The mean age of the students was 20.71 ± 1.79 years, 44.7% ranked midwifery among their first five programme choices, and 78.6% reported being happy when admitted to the programme. Satisfaction with midwifery education was moderately and positively correlated with a professional and autonomous perspective (r = 0.368, p < 0.001). Professional belonging was weakly and positively correlated with satisfaction with midwifery education (r = 0.239, p < 0.001) and with a professional and autonomous perspective (r = 0.138, p = 0.043). The perceived impact of education on professional perspective was not significantly correlated with these variables. Fourth-year students had higher satisfaction with midwifery education than first-year students. Professional belonging was also weakly associated with age. These findings indicate that educational satisfaction, professional perceptions, and selected student characteristics are associated with professional belonging; however, the cross-sectional design does not permit causal inferences.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF HERBAL ANTIMICROBIAL GEL CONTAINING APRAJITA CLITORIA TERNATEA L.
abstract: Skin infections caused by pathogenic microorganisms remain a major healthcare concern, and the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance has highlighted the need for safer and more effective topical therapies. Herbal medicines have gained considerable attention because of their broad therapeutic potential, low toxicity, and improved patient acceptability. The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate a herbal antimicrobial gel containing the ethanolic extract of Clitoria ternatea L. (Aprajita). Fresh flowers of Clitoria ternatea were collected, authenticated, shade-dried, powdered, and extracted using ethanol. The extract was incorporated into a Carbopol-based gel using suitable excipients to obtain a stable topical formulation. The prepared gel was evaluated for its physicochemical properties, including appearance, homogeneity, pH, viscosity, spreadability, extrudability, washability, and stability. Antimicrobial activity was assessed against selected pathogenic microorganisms using a standard microbiological method. The formulated gel exhibited acceptable physical characteristics, good consistency, suitable pH for topical application, satisfactory spreadability, and excellent stability throughout the study period. The formulation demonstrated promising antimicrobial activity, indicating the presence of bioactive phytoconstituents in the ethanolic extract of Clitoria ternatea. These findings suggest that the developed herbal gel has potential as a safe and effective topical antimicrobial formulation for the management of superficial skin infections. Further preclinical and clinical investigations are recommended to establish its therapeutic efficacy and long-term safety.
authors: Priya Singh1*, Dr. Paras Kumar Prajapati2, Dr. Pushpendra Kannojia3, Ms. Anshika Chaudhary4

title: Etiological and immunological aspects of equine hoof canker
abstract: Chronic equine proliferative pododermatitis (canker) is a hypertrophic hoof disease characterized by excessive proliferation of horn-producing tissues resulting from dyskeratosis of keratinocytes. Since its etiology remains unknown, this study investigated potential etiological agents and evaluated biochemical and immunological profiles. Ten horses with hoof canker and ten healthy controls of the Norik of Muran breed were included. Dermatophytes and bovine papillomavirus 1 and 2 (BPV 1/2) were not detected. Candida glabrata was the most frequently identified species in both affected and healthy groups. In horses with canker, Aspergillus fumigatus , Mucor spp., and Trichosporon spp. were also detected. Biochemical analysis showed significantly higher creatine kinase myoglobin binding activity in affected horses compared to controls (12.58 ± 5.86 vs. 4.11 ± 1.57; p < 0.01), with a slight increase in aspartate aminotransferase activity. Principal component analysis revealed substantial overlap between healthy and affected groups. Immunologically, monocyte phagocytic activity was significantly reduced in affected horses (83.78% ± 3.40 vs. 90.26% ± 2.88; p < 0.001). Affected horses had increased CD4 + (Th) lymphocyte counts and a higher CD4 + :CD8 + ratio ( p < 0.01), along with higher IgM + B lymphocyte levels (27.20% ± 8.23 vs. 18.51% ± 4.53; p < 0.05). Serum IgG levels were also significantly elevated (11.15 ± 3.42 vs. 5.88 ± 1.91 mg/mL; p < 0.001). These results indicate stimulation of adaptive cellular and humoral immune responses in canker-affected horses. However, the lack of consistent pathogen detection suggests that the precise etiology of hoof canker remains unresolved and requires further investigation.

title: Flexural Performance and Surface Hardness of Filler-Modified PMMA Designed for Denture Base Applications
abstract: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) is widely used in denture base fabrication; however, its relatively low flexural strength (FS) and durability limit long-term clinical performance. Reinforcing with nanofillers such as Halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) has emerged as a promising strategy to enhance the material's mechanical properties. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of different HNT loadings on the FS and surface hardness (VH) of PMMA denture base composites. PMMA composites were prepared using a heat-polymerised resin reinforced with treated HNTs at concentrations of 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 wt.%. To achieve uniform dispersion, the nanofillers were ultrasonically dispersed in methyl methacrylate before conventional polymerisation; the filler distribution and the effectiveness of silane functionalisation were examined through morphological and microchemical characterisation using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). Mechanical performance was assessed by determining FS via the three-point bending test, while VH was measured using the Vickers hardness method. Statistical analysis one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) followed by Tukey’s post hoc test, with significance set at p < 0.05 was performed, confirming that incorporating silane-treated HNTs significantly affected both tested properties (p < 0.05), with the highest values for FS (98.1 MPa) and hardness (20.20 kg/mm 2 ) observed at 5 wt% HNT loading, representing substantial improvements over unmodified PMMA. At higher concentrations (7-9 wt.%), a decline in properties was observed, attributed to nanoparticle agglomeration and reduced interfacial efficiency. HNT reinforcement effectively enhances the mechanical performance of PMMA denture base materials, with 5 wt.% identified as the optimal concentration. These findings support the potential application of HNT-reinforced PMMA to improve durability and clinical longevity of denture prostheses.
venue: International Journal of Biomedical Materials Research

title: PHENYLKETONURIA: AN OVERVIEW OF PATHOPHYSIOLOGY, DIAGNOSIS, AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: Phenylketonuria is an autosomal inborn error of metabolism characterized predominantly by dysfunctional phenylalanine (L-alpha-amino-beta-phenylpropionic acid) metabolism due to defects in phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) activity. Because of elevated levels of phenylalanine and low levels of tyrosine, neurologial symptoms and other system effects are produced. PKU has a variable worldwide prevalence that is modulated by ethnicity and geographic region. This disorder is usually linked with a destructive mutation in the PAH gene, while hyperphenylalaninemia may also result from an error in tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) metabolism. Elevated phenylalanine and its products can influence the central nervous system by acting as inhibitors of the large neutral amino acids transporter 1 (LAT1), altering neurotransmitters availability, compromising protein synthesis in the brain and generating oxidative stress. PKU may lead to severe intellectual disability, such as behavioral problems, seizures, microcephaly, hypopigmentation, as well as musty odour. A mothers' PKU may also have the opportunity to cause high risk of negative fetal outcomes with such possibilities of having microcephaly, disability, intelligence disability, growth retardation and even congenital heart defects. Identification with the help of newborn screening method with biochemical confirmation, and BH4 disorder evaluation is crucial for appropriate management. The main treatment for PKU will remain dietary phenylalanine restriction supported by medical formula and other amino acid supplements. Sapropterin and pegvaliase are included in pharmacological approaches, whereas gene therapy, enzyme therapy, microbial therapy, mRNA therapy, and red cell therapy serve as novel medical plans. Comprehensive Management and Early Diagnosis of phenylalanine level is very essential to decrease the risks related to this disease.
authors: Komalba Sarvaiya1, Sapna Desai2*, Satyajit Sahoo2, Rashmi Rajeghorpade3, Archana Kaushik3, Tejas Patel4, D. B. Meshram5
